description: Don Dimadón, dueño del Domodin de Dismdale, debía ampliar su estadio para el Super Bowl 2027 y faltaba dinero. Rumbo a OFC en Olancho halló tierras fértiles, pero los agricultores avisaron: la lluvia es impredecible y el suelo se agota. Nace el Equipo Don Dimadón: unimos datos de NASA sobre lluvia, temperatura y humedad del suelo con datos locales para explorar rotaciones de cultivo que protejan el suelo y ahorren agua.
summary: Crop Compass is a bilingual web tool that helps farmers in Choluteca, in Honduras' Dry Corridor, and the technicians who support them, decide what and when to plant. Many plant with borrowed money. It reduces the risk of losing that investment. Every day, a pipeline turns NASA Earth observation data into a traffic light per municipality and crop (maize, beans, sorghum): green, yellow, red or gray. The light comes from soil moisture, 7-day rain, heat and the official sowing window, and official COPECO/NHC alerts override it. The tool also compares each zone's real rain onset with the traditional calendar. It compares sowing and rotation strategies with a profitability estimate in local units (mz, qq, lempiras) and gives a 1-minute radio bulletin. Paco, an assistant, answers only from the published data. Every reading shows its source, its date and the note "may contain errors, consult an expert". Stale data turns gray and is never shown as green. It is decision support for the agricultural technician, not a replacement.
details:
A daily traffic light per municipality and crop, a rain-onset calendar versus reality, a sowing catalog by zone, a strategy and rotation comparison with a profitability estimate, a radio bulletin, Paco (an assistant answering only from published data), and optional accounts to save fields and a field passport.


How: a Python pipeline (GitHub Actions, daily) pulls NASA POWER and builds static JSON. Next.js 15 + TypeScript, next-intl (es/en), MapLibre GL, Recharts, Supabase (auth + RLS), Vercel. Paco runs on Groq (gpt-oss-120b) with fixed tools and an output guard.


Creative and considered: no invented data (missing data shows "not enough data"); gray over stale; risk shown with color + icon + text + voice for low literacy; local units; one notice per screen; offline-friendly radio format; designed to support DICTA technicians, not replace them.
